question.problem: Find the slope of the tangent to the curve $y=\operatorname{cot}⁡(2x)$ at the point $(\frac{\pi }{8},1).$
question.worked_solution:
First, the slope of $y=f(x)$ at $x=\frac{\pi }{8}$ is given by ${f}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{8}).$

We will calculate ${f}^{′}(x)$ using the chain rule. First, we express $f(x)$ as the composite function

$$
f=\operatorname{cot}⁡u,\,u=2x.
$$

Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}u}=-{csc}^{2}⁡u\,\text{and}\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=2.
$$

We now apply the chain rule, and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & =-{csc}^{2}⁡u\cdot (2) \\  & =-2{csc}^{2}⁡(2x).\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluating at $x=\frac{\pi }{8}$, we find 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{8}) & =-2{csc}^{2}⁡(2\cdot \frac{\pi }{8}) \\  & =-2{csc}^{2}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}) \\  & =-2\cdot {(\sqrt{2})}^{2} \\  & =-4\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of $y=f(x)$ at $x=\frac{\pi }{8}$ is $-4.$
